overview: Black meets 1.g4 with 1...f5, challenging the g-pawn at once. If White takes with 2.gxf5, Black gets open lines and quick development at the cost of a pawn. If White ignores it, Black can take on g4 or fight for the centre. I am unsure which side the name refers to, and reason from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn on f5 and consolidate

black_ideas.idea: Use the open lines and develop quickly

typical_structures.structure: Open lines after the pawn exchange on f5

character.notes: Immediate pawn tension and open lines make for sharp play.

gambit.notes: If White captures on f5, Black is a pawn down and can leave it that way for development.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider the pawn offer insufficient.

character.reason: Pawn tension and open files make the play forcing.

gambit.reason: Black offers the f-pawn after gxf5.

soundness.reason: The pawn offer probably gives too little.

structure.reason: Pawns come off and files open.

level.reason: A Dubious line is never Beginner.

plans.reason: Black aims for quick development in return for the pawn.
